snippet.title: Agentive Audit Automation by Daniel Alberson | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
AI is changing how audit work gets done, but auditor judgment remains at the center.

In this Miles Masterclass course, Daniel Alberson explores how agentive audit automation can help modernize audit workflows by using AI to execute repeatable procedures, extract information from documents, match support to selections, flag exceptions, and prepare results with source citations.

The course explains where AI can support audit teams and where human judgment must remain essential, including risk assessment, materiality, evidence evaluation, and final conclusions. Rather than treating AI as a simple chatbot, Daniel frames it as an agentic workflow engine that helps auditors move from manual execution to focused review.

Through practical demonstrations, learners will see how AI can be applied to grant revenue testing, expense testing, and financial statement review. The course highlights how AI can support evidence gathering, transaction tracing, classification testing, cut-off testing, exception identification, and stronger audit documentation.

snippet.title: 14 Years of Business Advice in 60 Seconds
snippet.description:
Had a convo with a young founder who was “stuck” this morning. 

Here was my parting advice:

1) Change directions less. 
2) Stick with things long enough to see if it really worked. And if you don’t know yet. Then keep doing it. 
3) The more stable you are the more stable your team will be
4) You can attract and retain talent proportional to your personal growth
5) Your business is simple, don’t complicate it.
6) Focusing on getting better will make you bigger. But focusing on getting bigger will only spread you to thin.
7) Raise your people standards. 
8) Build from the customer backwards to money, not the other way around.
9) Remember you’re gonna die and it’s not gonna matter so don’t stress so much - you’ve already won.

snippet.title: JWT Token Explained So Easy Even Newbies Get It!
snippet.description:
JWT Token Explained, Even Beginners/Juniors Get it!

Ever wondered how JWT token works? How your app keeps users authenticated without storing passwords on every request? 🤔

This visual perfectly breaks down JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication — a secure, stateless way to handle user sessions in modern web and mobile apps.

Here’s the flow 👇
1️⃣ The client logs in with username & password.
2️⃣ The server verifies credentials and creates a JWT — containing user claims, metadata, and a signature.
3️⃣ The client stores the token (usually in localStorage or cookies) and sends it with every request via the Authorization header.
4️⃣ The server validates the token’s signature to confirm it’s authentic, then grants access to protected resources.

Each JWT has 3 parts:

🟩 Header: Defines the type and signing algorithm (HMAC, RSA, etc.)
🟦 Payload: Holds user info and claims
🟩 Signature: Verifies integrity & authenticity

💡 Pro tip: Always use HTTPS and short token lifetimes — and refresh tokens securely to reduce risk of token theft.

Perfect for developers building APIs, microservices, or single-page apps (SPA) with frameworks like Laravel, Node.js, Django, Vue, or React.

snippet.title: Database Scaling Tricks and Techniques  for Performance Optimization #programming #database #mysql
snippet.description:
Database Scaling Techniques Explained | Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling, Caching, Indexing & Performance Optimization🚀

As your application grows, so does your data — and eventually, your database becomes the bottleneck. In this video, we walk through the most effective database scaling strategies used in real-world systems like SaaS platforms, fintech applications, and high-traffic APIs.

Whether you're a backend developer, software engineer, or system architect, this video helps you understand how to scale databases safely, efficiently, and cost-effectively — without downtime or degraded performance.

What You’ll Learn - Storyline

We start with a common problem:
Your app works perfectly at 1,000 users — but crashes at 100,000. Why?

Then we walk step-by-step through the evolution of database scaling, covering:

✅ Vertical Scaling (Scale Up)
Adding CPU, RAM, and faster storage — when it works, when it doesn’t, and its real limits.
✅ Query Optimization & Indexing
How to reduce slow queries using indexes, LIMIT clauses, joins optimization, and materialized views.
✅ Caching Strategies (Redis, Memcached)
How caching reduces database load and improves response times for high-traffic systems.
✅ Connection Pooling & Concurrency Control
How modern backend systems avoid database overload under heavy traffic using pooling and throttling.
✅ Horizontal Scaling (Scale Out)
Sharding, read replicas, and database partitioning — how large systems like Netflix and Shopify scale globally.

At end, you’ll understand when to scale vertically, when to shard horizontally, and how to combine caching, indexing, and replication for massive performance gains.

🎯 Who This Video Is For

- Backend Developers 
- Database Engineers (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB)
- Software Architects & DevOps Engineers
- Startup Founders building scalable SaaS platforms
- Interview prep for system design & backend roles

snippet.title: Is AI Orchestration a Job of the Future?
snippet.description:
Is an AI campaign orchestrator a job, a marketing job of the near future? One where it’s just you and agents running entire campaigns?

Had this thought when I was prepping for a discussion with marketing students and looking for an example to build. 

Example of a Spring Study Break campaign for a local coffee shop

This is what I think it may look like:
1. Use your favourite LLM to ideate a campaign idea and how sub-agents can help build that campaign
I used both Claude and ChatGPT, and how it create for the folder structure including: 
Agents.MD (Guides overall process) - similar to Claude.MD
Built the Skills - You probably want to spend time here
What I didn’t have is a brand Guideline or writing guide skill which if you haven’t already, create that SKILL!

2. Claude Code or Codex to create subagents to help you with:
Strategy
Audience insights
Copywriting
Creative Direction
Offer/Redemption operations

1. Have CC or Codex help build SKILLS for each agent. Literally go for a walk and have it ask you until it has all the information it needs to build the right SKILLS for the job. 

2. Once the sub-agents have completed their work, I now have everything from audience insights, the creative direction, the final campaign, the redemption flow, and even the strategy. 
I'm definitely simplifying things here because you’re probably we're going to spend a good amount of time reviewing, going over, and tailoring, fine-tuning all these outputs.
3. Now you should have some sort of brand guidelines, colours, logo, and so on but I didn't. What I did was I just went over to the SAIT website and took the colours. 

4. Then I went over to Google Stitch Google Stitch and asked it to help me build campaign ads, campaign landing page both the mobile and desktop version, using the brand colors. Literally copy and pasted a lot of these outputs. And you can upload any images and brand information as starting points too
5. Talka bout Prototype and how you can edit it all, QR code, export 
6. And I dialed in landing page copy with design all prototyped and ready for production. And if I didn't know how to code or didn't have time, I could either send it to a developer or vibe code it myself using AI studio 
7. Then everything in Stitch I can port over to Luma Labs and create a vertical video ad really quickly.

I was looking at the outputs of this entire campaign and it took me under an hour to get all the outputs. Previously, Campaign like this with all the outputs would have taken weeks if not months to build out.

I also know I'm just doing it with one or two iterations Google Stitch and Luma Labs. It is probably much more on your campaigns but you can still severely cut down take time to get an output done. 

In terms of cost, Google Stitch is free for now but there are rate limits. Luma Labs costs $30 and then whether you're on Codex or Claude Code depends on the plan that you're on. But even if you're on the max plan with the two models plus an extra, let's say, the pro plan with Luma Labs, which is 300 a month, that's a pretty good deal to be creating campaigns. 

Anyway how would you have used AI differently? Is an AI campaign orchestrator a I'll be the future?

It's still a job reduction In the long run but it's not laying off people today or in the near future. To say that AI can replace people doesn't make any sense because Even though AI could do the tasks, there's more to a job than just specific tasks.

For the most part people are very happy to get rid of the monotonous repetitive tasks and pass them on to AI. There are employees who enjoy that type of activity That's what they've developed a specialty in. That's going to be a much more difficult discussion and decision because employers want to move that person on to different things than that task alone.
